 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in the Judgment and award dated 01.04.2021 passed in MVC No.854/2017 by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-XV, Vijayapura (for short 'the tribunal').

2. The facts leading to filing of the claim petition are that, on 30.07.2017 at about 6.30 p.m., near Shankar Dhaba on Tikota-Toravi road, the appellant/claimant was traveling in a Cruiser Jeep bearing registration No.KA-36/M-5326 being driven by its driver in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and at a curve near Tikota, the driver being unable to NC: 2025:KHC-K:5144 HC-KAR control the vehicle, turned turtle, resulted in an accident.

Due to the accident, the appellant/claimant sustained grievous injuries and took treatment in a hospital at Vijayapura and Bhimaraya S/O Siddappa Biradar vs Appasaheb And Anr on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182040904/
2

entities.text: Siddappa Biradar vs Appasaheb And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: also in the Hospital at Miraj.
Due to the injuries, the petitioner lost his left palm except thumb.
The petitioner filed claim petition seeking compensation.
The tribunal after recording evidence has awarded compensation.
The claimant not satisfied with the award of compensation has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation as awarded by the tribunal.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that, the appellant/claimant was an agriculturist and due to the amputation of left palm except thumb, he cannot perform his agricultural activities and therefore, there is 100% disability and the tribunal has taken the disability at 25%, even though the Doctor has stated that, the claimant has 75% disability.

Learned counsel further submits that,
the compensation awarded for pain and suffering, food and nourishment, attendant charges, loss of income during laid up period and loss NC: 2025:KHC-K:5144 HC-KAR of amenities are on lower side.
He submits that, the appellant/claimant has taken treatment in Miraj and has spent more amount.
With this, he prayed for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance company would contend that, the tribunal has rightly taken the disability at 25%.
The compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads is also proper and correct.

6. Having heard the learned counsels, this Court has perused the impugned Judgment and award,
and the trial Court records.
7.
The photograph at Ex.P.7 indicates that, except thumb, other portion of the left palm has been amputed.
As per Sl.No.7 of Part II of Schedule I of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is 50% for loss of four fingers of one hand.

entities.text: Sl.No.7 of Part II of Schedule I
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The appellant/claimant was an agriculturist and due to the injury he cannot perform his agricultural work.

The Doctor who examined the appellant/claimant had issued disability certificate-Ex.P.16,
wherein, it is stated that, the disability is 75%.
The said Doctor NC: 2025:KHC-K:5144 HC-KAR has also been examined as P.W.2.
If a person has lost his four fingers of one hand, he is not able to do agricultural work.
Considering the same, the disability as stated by P.W.2-Doctor at 75% is requires to be taken.
The tribunal has not taken the future prospects.

Considering the age of the appellant/claimant as 40 years as on the date of the accident, he is entitle to future prospects at 25%
in view of the decision in the case of Jagdish Vs. Mohan and others, reported in (2018) 4 SCC 571.
8.

In view of the above, the claimant is entitle for loss of future earnings as under:
Rs.10,250/- + 25% = Rs.12,812/-
Rs.12,812/- X 12 X 14 X 75% = Rs.16,14,312/-

sentences.text: Considering the fact that, there is amputation of left palm except thumb, the award of compensation under the head of pain and suffering in a sum of Rs.40,000/- and loss of amenities in a sum of Rs.30,000/- by the tribunal are on lower side.

Considering the injury and disability, the appellant/claimant is entitle to a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- each under the head of 'pain and suffering'
and 'loss of amenities'.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5144 HC-KAR 10.
The claimant was admitted in the hospital for 15 days in Miraj.
Considering the same, the attendant charges and conveyance charges by the tribunal in a sum of Rs.7,500/- is on lower side and he is entitle to a sum of Rs.15,000/-.
11. In view of the amputation of left palm except thumb, he is entitle to loss of income during laid up period for six months in a sum of Rs.61,500/- (Rs.10,250/- X 6 months).

The tribunal has rightly awarded medical expenses of Rs.84,378/- and food and nourishment, special diet in a sum of Rs.10,000/-
12.

In view of the above, the appellant/claimant is entitle to total compensation as under:
Sl.No. Heads of compensation Compensation awarded by this Court 1 Loss of future earnings Rs.16,14,312/- 2
Pain and
sufferings
Rs.1,50,000/- 3 Medical expenses Rs.84,378/- 4 Food and nourishment Rs.10,000/-

5 Attendant charges Rs.15,000/- 6 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.61,500/-
(Rs.10,250/- X 6 months)

7 Loss of amenities Rs.1,50,000/-
 Total Rs.20,85,190/-
 NC: 2025:KHC-K:5144  HC-KAR  13.
The appellant/claimant is entitle to total compensation of Rs.20,85,190/- as against Rs.6,33,128/- as awarded by the tribunal.

(iii) The respondent No.2-Insurance company shall deposit the award amount with interest within a period of eight weeks from this day, failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum;
